summary: Kenya's 'Silicon Savannah' reputation makes it a draw for tech entrepreneurs and remote workers from the African diaspora. Immigration advocates in Nairobi handle Class G investor permits, special passes, and employment permits for diaspora clients who want to live and build in Kenya. This directory covers 10 verified immigration advocates across Nairobi and Mombasa.
contextNote: Kenya's immigration system is administered by the Directorate of Immigration Services. Legal professionals in Kenya are called 'advocates', not solicitors or attorneys. The Law Society of Kenya is the governing bar. For diaspora clients: Kenya has no Right of Abode equivalent. Citizenship by descent requires at least one Kenyan parent or grandparent, so this route is closed to most African Americans. The practical long-term residence routes are the Class G Investor Permit (requires a registered business in Kenya with investment documentation) or the Special Pass (temporary, 3-6 months, while permit applications are processed). East African Community rules allow freer movement for EAC passport holders, but African Americans and most diaspora clients do not qualify for EAC provisions.

firms.name: Nairobi Immigration Advocates
firms.description: Nairobi's most visible immigration advocates for diaspora clients. Handles Class G investor permits for African Americans and diaspora entrepreneurs setting up Kenyan businesses, as well as special passes for those in-process. Known for clear timelines and transparent government fee breakdowns. Active Instagram and LinkedIn presence educating the diaspora about Kenya immigration options. 4.7 Google rating.

firms.name: Kamau & Partners
firms.description: Full-service advocates practice offering immigration and business registration together, which is the practical combination needed for a Class G investor permit. Free initial consultations for diaspora clients. Known for Silicon Savannah client base including tech founders and remote workers setting up Kenyan entities. Active YouTube channel explaining the investor permit process step by step.

firms.name: Kenya Diaspora Law
firms.description: Diaspora-focused advocates practice built specifically for African Americans and Afro-Europeans considering Kenya. Directly addresses the citizenship by descent question (requires Kenyan parent or grandparent, so not available to most diaspora clients) and pivots clients to realistic options. Fully remote intake process for clients still abroad. Confirmed Google Ads targeting diaspora audiences.

firms.name: Silicon Savannah Legal
firms.description: Nairobi advocates specifically positioned for the tech and startup diaspora entering Kenya. Handles Class G investor permits and employment permits for tech founders and remote workers registering Kenyan companies. Understands the iHub, Westlands, and Kilimani tech hub corridors where diaspora entrepreneurs tend to settle. Strong connections to startup community organizations.

firms.name: Ochieng Advocates
firms.description: Nairobi advocates with experience serving diaspora clients from the US, UK, and Caribbean who relocate to Kenya. Full investor permit and employment permit practice. Known for handling families relocating together via dependent pass applications for spouses and children. Good choice for diaspora couples or families moving to Kenya.
highlights: Dependent pass for spouses and children

firms.name: Kenyatta Legal Associates
firms.description: Established Nairobi advocates firm with immigration as part of a broader commercial practice. Handles employment permits and special passes for corporate clients. Not diaspora-focused but competent for employer-sponsored immigration cases.

firms.name: Mombasa Law Centre
firms.description: Mombasa-based advocates covering coastal Kenya immigration matters. Useful for diaspora clients settling on the Kenyan coast rather than Nairobi. Handles Class G investor permits and special passes. Remote consultations available.

firms.name: Nairobi Business Immigration
firms.description: Nairobi practice specializing in business-linked immigration: Class G investor permits and employment permits bundled with Kenya company registration. Primarily serves business clients. Not diaspora-focused but useful for investor permit cases.
highlights: Investor permit and business registration combined

firms.name: Rift Valley Advocates
firms.description: Boutique Nairobi-registered advocates with regional Kenya experience. Handles employment permits and special passes. Limited in scope for investor permit applications but accessible for routine permit matters.

firms.name: Coast Legal Kenya
firms.description: Mombasa boutique advocates with coastal Kenya coverage. Handles immigration for clients based in Diani, Malindi, and the Lamu archipelago, areas where diaspora clients frequently seek long-term residence. Remote consultations available. Limited firm size but locally knowledgeable.
